Historians thus have developed a complex understanding of how Mongol expansion triggered new forms of globalization, whether in terms of long-distance commercial exchange, epidemic disease circulation, state formation, or religious conversion. This course offers an introduction to the study of not just the Mongols, but a host of other Eurasian societies that had to reckon with Mongol power.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Asia and the Birth of Global Capitalism, 1400-1850
courses.description: This course studies the economies of early modern Asia through the perspective of both Asian actors and the European East India Companies (Portuguese, Dutch, English, French, etc.). Early modern Asia was the epicenter of the early modern global economy, with China and India responsible for 50% of world manufacturing output. In order to enter into this world, Europeans developed a number of strategies. Despite their ready use of coercion, Europeans remained marginal actors in early modern Asia. Towards the end this course studies how the North Atlantic replaced Asia as the center of the world economy around 1800.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Ethics and Business in Africa
courses.description: Explores sub-Saharan Africa both as a historical site of exploitative, extractive labor practices and initiatives to make business more ethical. Starting in the precolonial period, it considers topics such as ending the slave trades, the foundations of colonial economies, development projects postindependence, and the use of conflict minerals. Previously offered as HIST 540. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Empire, Race, and Resistance
courses.description: This course introduces students to the history of empire, the role of race in creating and sustaining it, and the ways that people have resisted the imposition of outsider control. It will also introduce students to the methods historians use to understand the past.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Global World Order from World War II to the Present
courses.description: This course deals with the establishment and development of the rules-based global order towards the end of World War II. The course will help us to understand the driving forces, fears, and ideas that have led to the post-war global order and the emergence of new states and international organizations. We will discuss this system as well as the forces of nationalism, imperialism, just war ideas, great power theories, and many related themes.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Dictators and Democracy: Autocracy and "the People" from Antiquity to Today
courses.description: This course will trace the relationship between individual power and the will of "the people" from European Antiquity to its manifestations around the world today. It will explore how autocrats legitimate their power based on the notion of popular representation.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Dictators in the 20th Century
courses.description: Dictators are typically viewed as brutal individuals who wield absolute power over their state. But, are these stereotypes true? The aims of this seminar are to dispel the myths that shroud dictators, to give students a more nuanced understanding of dictatorships in the 20th century, and to introduce them to biographies as a genre of historical writing.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Fascist Challenge in Europe, 1918-1945
courses.description: The course focus on theories on fascism, national cultures of fascism (e.g. Nazi Germany, Fascist Italy, Hungary) as well as selected topics which are essential to understand the attraction and functioning of fascist movements and regimes since 1918 in Europe (e.g. racism, war, culture, charismatic leadership).

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Migration
courses.description: This course places the act of human migration at the center of modern history. Through case studies of various migrant groups, students will explore important questions at the center of migration history: why some people move and some stay; how the movements of people shape political, economic, social, and cultural life; and how ideas about migration, immigration, nation, and place have developed historically.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Comparative Empires in the Modern World
courses.description: This course will examine the history of how empires uses grand claims of civilizational, moral, and religious claims in their foreign policy and grand strategy with a focus on the British, Ottoman, and Japanese imperial strategies. The course will also discuss contemporary legacies of British-Ottoman confrontation in WWI and British-Japanese conflict in WWII.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Environmental History and Computer Science: Mapping the Black Sea
courses.description: This course uses the digital technology of the 21st century to analyze the interactions of past civilizations by creating a "story map" that will visualize the ebbs and flows of peoples and civilizations throughout a geographical place, the Black Sea.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Great Depression and Its Legacies
courses.description: This course will assess visions for social change during the Great Depression, evaluate New Deal reforms, and address the legacy Depression-era Americans made on institutions and succeeding generations. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Cinema, Culture, and Society
courses.description: After the First World War, culture in Germany became a forum for radical experimentation and a source of deep conflict. Through a consideration of art and literature, and with emphasis on mass cultural forms such as film and newspapers, this course explores the complex relationships between politics and culture and how such relationships were understood and debated in both the Weimar Republic and Nazi Germany.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: War and Gender in Movies
courses.description: The course examines and compares the images of war and gender that movies from different time periods and countries propagate and explores the different factors that influence these images and thereby the perception and recollection of war. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: American Women's History to 1865
courses.description: This course will explore women's experiences in America from 1500 to 1865. Topics will include the ways in which women have shaped American politics, economy, society, and culture.

source.text: HIST 355. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | WGST 354 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: American Women's History, 1865 to the Present
courses.description: This course will examine the changing lives of women in the United States after 1865: Their contribution to economy, society, cultural change, and political struggles.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The U.S. South to 1865
courses.description: Economic, cultural, and social history of the antebellum South. The region's political history will serve as a supporting part of the study. Previously offered as HIST 586.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The New South
courses.description: This course explores the transformation of the South from the time of the Civil War and emancipation to the contemporary rise of the Sunbelt. Previously offered as HIST 587.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Early American Republic, 1789-1848
courses.description: The society and politics of the United States during the period dominated by President Andrew Jackson. Topics include economic development, the expansion of slavery, religion and reform, the changing roles of women, and the political movements associated with 'Jacksonian democracy.' Previously offered as HIST 563.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Ideas in Modern America
courses.description: This course surveys questions that have preoccupied leading thinkers and shaped intellectual culture in America since 1870. Themes include the problem of defining American identity, the clash between faith and reason, social injustice, the meaning of "modernity," the power and pitfalls of ideology, conceptions of human nature. Honors version available.

source.text: HIST 360. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER, RESEARCH.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, and Transgender Histories in the United States
courses.description: This course investigates the history of people who might today be defined as lesbian, gay, bisexual, or transgender (LGBT) in the United States. Key themes will include identity formation, culture, politics, medical knowledge, discrimination, and community.

source.text: HIST 361. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | WGST 360 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Baseball and American History
courses.description: Course explores the historical significance of baseball in American life, using the history of the game to investigate topics such as industrialization, urbanization, and immigration; conflicts between labor and capital; racial prejudice and integration; patriotism and American identity; evolving gender ideals; and the role of myth in American culture.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Popular Culture and American History
courses.description: Study of the popular arts and entertainments of the 19th and 20th centuries and the ways in which they illuminate the values, assumptions, aspirations, and fears of American society. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of American Business
courses.description: A survey of the rise and development of the major financial, commercial, manufacturing, and transportation enterprises that transformed the United States from an agricultural into a leading industrial nation.

source.text: HIST 364. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | MNGT 364 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Worker and American Life
courses.description: From the experience of colonial artisans to contemporary factory and office workers, organized and unorganized, this course examines the effect of the industrial revolution on the American social and political landscape.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: North Carolina History before 1865
courses.description: The history of North Carolina from the original Indian cultures to the end of the Civil War. Important topics include colonization, the American Revolution, evangelical religion, slavery, economic and political reform, the rise of sectionalism, and the Civil War.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: North Carolina's Unfinished Democracy
courses.description: This course explores the long, unfinished struggle for democracy in North Carolina, from the pre-Civil War era to the modern day. Important topics include Emancipation and Reconstruction, agrarian protests, Black disfranchisement and Jim Crow segregation, industrialization and labor protests, campaigns for civil rights and equal citizenship, Latino immigration, and 20th-century politics.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: U.S. War and Society to 1920
courses.description: This class examines the relationship between war, the U.S. military, and the social, cultural, and political history of the United States from the colonial era to the end of World War I. It analyzes the military as a social institution and how war has shaped American history, broadly speaking.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: U.S. War and Society Since 1920
courses.description: This class examines the relationship between war, the U.S. military, and the social, cultural, and political history of the United States from World War I to the present. It analyzes the military as a social institution and how war has shaped American history in this time span. It focuses primarily on World War II, the Vietnam War, and the War on Terror.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Iraq War
courses.description: The U.S. invasion of Iraq in 2003 was one of the most controversial and consequential foreign policy decisions of the 21st century. This course will help students understand the origins of the conflict, the basics of modern Iraqi history, the effects of the war in Iraq, the US, and the Middle East, and its legacies today.

source.text: HIST 370. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST. | PWAD 370 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Football and American History
courses.description: Course explores the popularity of football in American history and asks, "Why has the game mattered so much in this country?" We will also use the story of football to explore many of the larger storylines and controversies in this nation's past. We will focus on the class origins of college and professional football; racial prejudice, exclusion, and integration in the game; football and the evolving ideas about masculinity and womanhood; the role of the game in the promotion of a vigorous national identity; and the use of football stadiums as spaces to both legitimize and protest the political order.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of American Politics, 1932-Present
courses.description: This course explores the political history of the United States from the New Deal in the 1930s to the present. Topics include the trajectories of liberalism and conservatism and the origins of today's most protracted political debates--from McCarthyism to 9/11, from Watergate to Obamacare. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The United States in World War II
courses.description: A history of the United States in World War II (1941-1945): home front and military front.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The American West, 1800 to the Present
courses.description: A survey of the growth and development of the American West from the nineteenth century to the present as a culture, economy, and society. Considers the interactions between Native Americans and other people of different races, national origins and genders as agents and contributors to the forging of the American West.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Gender in America
courses.description: This course will explore how Americans from 1600 to the present have defined what is masculine and what is feminine and how they have constructed their identities around those definitions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of African Americans to 1865
courses.description: Survey of African American history to abolition of slavery in North America with some attention to experiences of people of African descent in Latin America and the Caribbean.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of African Americans, 1865 to Present
courses.description: Survey of African American history since emancipation in North America with some attention to experiences of people of African descent in Latin America and the Caribbean. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Slavery and the University
courses.description: This course explores the University of North Carolina's early history with relation to racial slavery. It is built around an archival research project that changes from term to term.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The History of the Civil Rights Movement
courses.description: This course examines the history of the modern African American civil rights movement, focusing on its development and processes, historical significance, and continuing legacy in the United States of America and abroad. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Big-Time College Sports and the Rights of Athletes, 1874 to the Present
courses.description: The evolution of college sports since the Harvard-McGill football game of 1874. Key turning points include the football crisis of 1905 and the creation of the NCAA, the reform efforts of the 1930s, the 1984 Supreme Court case on television money, and the emergence of an "athletes' rights" movement.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: America in the Sixties
courses.description: Through a variety of interconnected themes, this course focuses on the wide-ranging experiences of life in the United States of America during the 1960s to explain major shifts in postwar modern American history and explore the origins of contemporary American society. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: African American Women's History
courses.description: The course covers the history of black women in the United States from the 18th century to the present. It deals with such themes as work, family, community, sexuality, politics, religion, and culture. Previously offered as HIST/WGST 569.

source.text: HIST 385. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | WGST 382 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Chinese Strategic Thought: Antiquity to the Present
courses.description: This course will introduce undergraduates to Chinese strategic and military thought through the translated writings of some of China's most significant philosophers, intellectuals, and political leaders, from antiquity to the present. Students will explore historical characteristics of Chinese strategy and consider the influence of these ideas in current international relations.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Special Topics in History
courses.description: Subject matter will vary with instructor but will focus on some particular topic or historical approach. Course description available from departmental office. Closed to graduate students. Repeatable for credit. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Practical Introduction to Editing, Reviewing, and Publishing Historical Research: Traces Internship
courses.description: In this course, students will work as the assistant editors for Traces: The UNC-Chapel Hill Journal of History, collaborating with the graduate student editorial team and their faculty advisor to produce a peer-reviewed academic journal. Students will be introduced to the full academic publishing process, selecting which papers to accept/reject, working with accepted authors to refine their articles, and assisting in the maintenance of the website and creation of the physical journal.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 8 total credits. 8 total completions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Research Related Skills
courses.description: Subject matter will vary with instructor but will focus on some particular historical methodology, approach, and/or practice. Course description available from the departmental office.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Independent Study in History
courses.description: Permission of the department. Directed reading under the supervision of a faculty member.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Undergraduate Seminar in History
courses.description: The course is in general limited to 15 students. The subject matter will vary with the instructor. Each course will concern itself with a study in depth of some historical problem. Students will write a substantial research paper. Permission of the department. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Special Topics in History, FC-PAST
courses.description: Subject matter will vary with instructor but will focus on some particular topic or historical approach.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Beating the Market? A History of Communist Economies
courses.description: The goal of this course is both to highlight the varieties of Communist economies in Asia and Europe and the ways that ideology, violence, institution-building and competition have shaped their contours and trajectories. Students will gain a literacy in the methods of economic history, an appreciation for how economic equalities drive state policy, and a knowledge of how ideology and institutions are co-constitutive.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Family and Gender in Early Modern China and Korea
courses.description: This course explores family and kinship in early modern China and Korea through the lens of gender and sexuality. In particular, it invites students to think beyond the bias that women in premodern East Asia were victims of patriarchy to understand their active participation in their world-making as well as their dynamic imagination and expression through writing, working, learning, loving.

source.text: HIST 418. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | ASIA 418 , WGST 418 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Alexander
courses.description: The rise of Macedonia; the careers of Philip II and Alexander (with emphasis on the latter's campaigns); the emerging Hellenistic Age. The course integrates computer (including Web site) and audiovisual materials throughout.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Ancient Greek Warfare
courses.description: War and the warrior in the archaic and classical Greek world, seventh to the fourth centuries BCE. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Archaic Greece, 800-480 BCE
courses.description: HIST 225 strongly recommended. Topical approach to the social and cultural history of the ancient Greek city states, ca. 800-336 BCE.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Classical Greece (Sixth-Fourth Centuries BCE)
courses.description: HIST 225 strongly recommended. The life and times of the ancient Athenians from the sixth to fourth centuries BCE.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Roman History, 154 BCE-14 CE
courses.description: Explores the transformation from Republic to Principate. Conducted in considerable part by student reports and classroom discussions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Early Roman Empire, 14 CE-193 CE
courses.description: Focuses upon administrative, social, and economic themes. Conducted in considerable part by student reports and classroom discussions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Later Roman Empire, 193 CE-378 CE
courses.description: Focuses upon administrative, social, and economic themes. Conducted in considerable part by student reports and classroom discussions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Ancient Sexuality
courses.description: This course deals with the complex topic of ancient sexuality, which includes courtship, marriage, family structure, public and private morality, and law enforcement. In terms of historical method, this course teaches students how to discover evidence for social history in both diverse documentary and literary sources.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Medieval Church
courses.description: The nature and workings of the Western church between roughly 600 and 1300. Emphasis on the church "from within," organization, missionary strategies, liturgy, monasticism, popular religion.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Crusades
courses.description: Students in this course will examine Christian attitudes toward holy war, crusading, and other forms of coercive violence from the 11th until the 15th centuries, with a focus on the major crusades to the Holy Land.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Medieval England
courses.description: A consideration of England's origins, unification, and development as a national monarchy. Primary emphasis is on political, ecclesiastical, and cultural aspects.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Medieval University
courses.description: The origins and development of the university during the period 1100 to 1400; types of organization, curricula and degrees, intellectual life, town-gown and student-master relationships.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Aristocratic Culture in the Central Middle Ages
courses.description: This course has as its theme the lives of aristocratic men and women in western Europe between about 850 and 1200 CE. Discusses the nature of aristocratic identity, the trends that shaped the lives of aristocratic men and women, and the different roles of men and women within aristocratic culture.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Medieval Masculinities, 500-1200
courses.description: This course examines the multifaceted constructions of masculinity found in narrative texts produced in medieval western Europe. Focuses on topics such as gender relations, male self-fashioning, homosocial bonding, family structures. Sources studied range from epic and romance to chronicles and visual records. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Environmental China: Premodern Political Ecology
courses.description: This course explores the history of premodern China from an environmental perspective. Based on mini-lectures and intensive discussions, it investigates diverse modes and sites of human-nature interactions such as agriculture, forestry, marine activities, natural disasters, and landscape cultivation.

source.text: HIST 439. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-PAST, RESEARCH. | CHIN 439 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Gender in Indian History
courses.description: An analysis of the roles of women and men in Indian societies from the early to the modern periods. Topics include the cultural construction of gender and sexuality; beauty and bodily practices; gender and religion; gender and politics; race, imperialism, and gender. Previously offered as HIST/ASIA 556.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Beauty and the Body in Pre-Colonial Indian History
courses.description: This course will discuss theories of beauty and the body in Indian History (c. 3 - 17th centuries) and their relation to differing constructions of gender.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Religion, Co-existence, and Conflict in Pre-Colonial India
courses.description: This course traces the fascinating history of material, cultural, and theological exchanges and conflicts between individuals belonging to two of the world's major religions: Hinduism and Islam. Throughout the course we will also analyze how modern commentators have selectively used the past to inform their understandings of the present. Previously offered as HIST/ASIA 555.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Settler Colonialism in Global Perspective
courses.description: This seminar introduces the field of settler colonial studies and history. It investigates how settler colonial polities consolidated during and after the global "settler revolution," how they managed relations with the imperial metropole and dealt with the Indigenous populations, whose resistance, adaptation, survival and agency also feature.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Humanitarianism in Historical Perspective
courses.description: This seminar examines humanitarianism in global context around 1800, beginning with the formation of humanitarian movements dedicated to alleviating suffering and especially ending slavery. It traces the movement's complicated relationship to empire in the 19th century, and the professionalization of humanitarian aid in the 20th century.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Gender and the Law in United States History
courses.description: This course will explore how the law in America has defined and regulated gender and sexuality. Significant topics will range from marriage, reproduction and the family to suffrage, work, and social movements. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Women and Politics in the United States
courses.description: This course examines the history of women's involvement in the political process in the United States from the founding to the present. Students will examine women's historical role in the political process, the different ways that women have engaged as political actors (even when disenfranchised), and the issues that became defined as women's issues.

source.text: HIST 449. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER, FAD. | WGST 449 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Renaissance: Italy, Birthplace of the Renaissance, 1300-1550
courses.description: A study of the people, culture, and intellectual achievements of the Italian Renaissance with emphasis on the interaction between culture and society.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Mediterranean Societies and Economics in the Renaissance World
courses.description: A picture of Mediterranean social and economic life 1300 to 1600, with special focus on rural and urban society, family structure, patronage, work and wages, public and private finance.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Reformation
courses.description: Examines a movement of religious reform that shattered Latin Christendom and contributed many of the conditions of early modern Europe. Emphases: religious, political, social.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Holocaust, Genocide and Historical Methodology
courses.description: This seminar will familiarize students with foundational works of Holocaust historiography as well as with newer works that challenge old interpretations and methodologies. Throughout the course we will look at the mutual influences of historical writing and memory of the Holocaust as societies have come to terms with the dark past of the Second World War; the course will also examine historical writing as a form of representation and memory. Previously offered as HIST 743.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Liberalism, Socialism, and Fascism in Europe
courses.description: This seminar examines liberal, socialist, communist, and fascist political systems in Europe during the twentieth century by comparing and contrasting their ideologies and approaches to their citizens' welfare. The seminar compares European and US experiences, and also attends to conservative critiques of the expansion of government activity in the 1940s.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Europe and the World Wars, 1914-1945
courses.description: Europe and the experience of total war, with special focus on national conflicts; ideological conflicts among fascism, communism, and liberalism; and the dictatorships of Hitler and Stalin.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Global Evangelicalism since 1600
courses.description: This is a survey of evangelical Christianity from 1600 to the present. We will trace the roots of evangelicalism in post-Reformation Europe, its diverse expressions and political influence in modern Western culture, and its recent spread throughout the Global South.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Germany, 1806-1918: Politics, Society, and Culture
courses.description: This course examines the changes in German politics, culture, and society during the long 19th century, with a focus on the Anti-Napoleonic Wars and the following era of restoration, the Vormärz and the Democratic Revolution of 1848 to 1849, the German Unification of 1871 and the Wilhelmine Empire, and finally World War I. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Germany since 1918: Politics, Society, and Culture
courses.description: This course examines the changes in German politics, culture, and society during the 20th century, with a focus on the Weimar Republic, the Third Reich and World War II, the reshaping of East and West Germany since the post-war era, and the unification in 1989. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Modern European Intellectual History
courses.description: The main developments in European thought from the Enlightenment to the 20th century, with some attention to social context. Readings include Voltaire, Rousseau, Hegel, Marx, Tocqueville, Sand, Flaubert, Nietzsche, Freud. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Culture on the Move: Art, Empire, and Restitution since 1800
courses.description: This discussion-based course examines the systems of value that confer special status on the broad category of cultural property, then explores a number of case studies of art theft and restitution since the early 19th century, with an emphasis on art theft during World War II and that undertaken under the aegis of European colonialism.

source.text: HIST 468. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | ARTH 484 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: European Social History
courses.description: The social transformation of Europe from agrarian through postindustrial society, discussing population growth, family history, spread of education, class structure, social conflict, group ideologies, and mass politics, as well as everyday lives and popular lifestyles.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Britain in World Affairs: British Foreign Policy since World War II
courses.description: The course provides a historical, political, and socio-economic framework for understanding British history and politics in the 20th and 21st centuries. We will assess important turning points in domestic British politics, the main focus will be on Britain's foreign relations during both the Cold War and the post-Cold War years.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Feminism
courses.description: This course will examine the unprecedented surge of feminist thought and activism in the postwar United States. Course materials and discussions will trace feminists' varied conceptions of empowered womanhood and their expectations of the state, society at large, and each other. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Religion and Ethnicity
courses.description: The history of modern Eastern, East Central, and southeastern Europe has been shaped by the ethnic and religious diversity of the regions. This course examines experiences in the Russian, Habsburg, and Ottoman Empires and their successor states from the 19th century to the present day.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Revolution in Russia, 1900-1930
courses.description: A close study of Russia's age of revolution from the reign of the last tsar to the turbulent Stalin Revolution of 1929, with emphasis on the revolutions of 1917.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Stalin and After: The USSR, 1929-Present
courses.description: An in-depth examination of Soviet and post-Soviet history from 1929 to the present.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Female Sexualities
courses.description: Spanning the ancient, medieval, and modern West, this course explores normative and non-normative female sexualities, ideas about female bodies, and the regulation of female sexuality by families, religions, and states.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Russia's 19th Century: Cultural Splendor, Imperial Decay
courses.description: The diplomatic, military, and ideological confrontations with the West; the decline and fall of the Russian autocracy; the evolution of reform thought; and revolutionary opposition.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: From Communists to Capitalists: Eastern Europe since 1945
courses.description: An examination of the countries of Eastern Europe, their origins and development since World War II, their cohesion and conflict.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Russia, Eurasian Empire
courses.description: This course examines the development of the Russian Empire, from the Mongol conquest in the 13th century to the transformation of Imperial Russia in the Soviet Union after 1917.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Nation and Religion in Russia
courses.description: This course explores the role of nation and religion in shaping political, cultural, and social experience and change in Tsarist and Soviet Russia through the prism of Christianity, Islam, and Judaism.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Islam in Tsarist and Soviet Russia
courses.description: This course examines the role that Islam has played in the history of the Russian sphere--interior Russia, Siberia, the Caucasus, and Central Asia--from the 18th century to the present. Topics include methods of rule, social change, Islamic institutions, attempts to bureaucratize religion, and resistance.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: From Fiddler on the Roof to the Holocaust: East European and Soviet Jewish History
courses.description: Eastern Europe was one of the largest centers of Jewish civilization from premodern times to the Second World War, giving rise to important religious, cultural, and political developments in Jewish modernity. This course examines main developments of Jewish society from the late 18th century until the aftermath of the Holocaust.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Extremism, Terrorism, and Security in Postwar Europe
courses.description: In the debate on how to efficiently combat terrorism without abandoning the rule-of-law, it is often neglected that this is not a new problem. This course will examine European states' reactions to national and international terrorism since the 1960s. Case studies will include Germany, Italy, and the United Kingdom. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Global Intellectual History
courses.description: This seminar studies the circulation, exchange, translation, reception, and adaptation of political, social, and cultural ideas across time and space. After considering systems of knowledge in Asia, Africa, and the Americas, the seminar explores reactions to European empire. Themes include (de)coloniality, modernity, development, conceptions of nationality, race, and civilizations. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The History of the 2008 Financial Crisis
courses.description: This course explores the 2008 financial crisis as a window into the longer history of global capitalism. We consider the construction of the sub-prime mortgage market, mass securitization, deregulation, and the interconnected nature of global finance, as well as the historical development of crises within financial capitalism. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Special Topics in History
courses.description: Subject matter will vary with instructor but will focus on some particular topic or historical approach. Course description available from the departmental office. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 9 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Internship in History
courses.description: Permission of the director of undergraduate studies. A supervised internship at an organization or institution engaged in the promotion of historical studies or the collection and preservation of historical documents and artifacts.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Directed Readings in History
courses.description: Permission of the director of undergraduate studies. Directed reading and relevant writing, supervised by a member of the department, in a selected field of history.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Independent Research in History
courses.description: Permission of the director of undergraduate studies. Directed primary source research and production of a research project, supervised by a member of the department. Prior coursework in the selected field is recommended.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Gender, Empire, and Nation
courses.description: This course explores the growing body of research on gender, empire, and nation/nationalism in modern European history by focusing on problems of national belongings and citizenship, state and nation building and empire formation, and the gendered discourses and representations of nation and empire.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Grand Strategy
courses.description: What separates successful states from failed ones? This course explores grand strategy as the long-term planning and execution of a nation's political, military, and economic goals. This course examines the theory and history of grand strategy in international affairs over the last 2,500 years. By looking at a series of thinkers, practitioners, and case studies, it asks what distinguishes good strategy from bad strategy, how circumstances can empower and constrain individuals, and whether we can identify strategic principles that endure across time.

source.text: HIST 502. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-PAST. | SCLL 500 , PWAD 500 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Geopolitical Rivalry, Development, and Global Capitalism, 1900-1950
courses.description: This course uses geopolitics, empire, and development as prisms to examine the economic history of the globe from the First World War to the dawn of the postcolonial age. We first first trace how states and populations the world over grappled with the economic effects stemming from the First World War itself and the breakdown of the prewar order. From we move into the interwar period and analyze the attempts by various actors in US, Europe and Asia to contest the economic realities of the 1920s/30s. Thereafter, we study total war economies and economic reform in the age of decolonization.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Europe and Humanitarian Aid since 1945: Concepts, Actors, Practices
courses.description: This seminar offers students an insight into the role of Europe within the global regime of humanitarian aid. After looking at the history and at theoretical definitions of humanitarianism, the course will examine a variety of case studies to assess the changing role of Europe in the post-war era.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The World History of Slavery
courses.description: This course considers slavery in comparative context, from ancient times to the present and across the world. It offers a chronological narrative and raises themes for comparison, including women in slavery and challenges to slavery. This approach allows for a wide view of this pervasive institution and develops analytical skills.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Human Rights in the Modern World
courses.description: This course looks at the international history of human rights from the Enlightenment to the present and considers how human rights ideas first emerged, how they evolved, and how they became so influential. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: 9/11 in World History
courses.description: This course focuses on three great decolonization movements-Communism, Nationalism, and Islamism-in the postcolonial Islamic world, in an attempt to understand the impact of the 9/11/2001 terrorists attacks on the social, political, and cultural life of Muslims in predominantly Islamic countries and diasporic communities in the West. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Monuments and Memory
courses.description: Explores the role of monuments in the formation of cultural memory and identity, both nationally and globally. Topics include the construction of identities in and through public spaces, commemoration of both singular individuals and ordinary citizens, and the appearance of new types of post-traumatic monuments in the 20th century.

source.text: HIST 514. | 3 Credits. | FC-AESTH or FC-PAST. | ARTH 514 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Historical Time
courses.description: This course explores the ways in which Western historians and other students of the past from Adam Ferguson to Stephen Jay Gould have conceptualized and packaged historical time. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Gender, Military, and War
courses.description: This course introduces students to new research on the history of gender, the military, and war in a comparative perspective. It explores the interrelations between changing military systems, types of warfare, the gender order, as well as political, social, and cultural currents in modern history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Colloquium in World Military History
courses.description: Reading colloquium in world military history, emphasizing Europe, focusing on the most significant issues, methods, and approaches in the field today.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of the Andes
courses.description: This course offers a survey of the history of the Andean region. The primary focus will be either the pre-Inca, Inca, and colonial periods or the 19th and 20th centuries, depending on the instructor.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of the Caribbean
courses.description: Thematic approach to the history of the West Indies, with emphasis on the period from European conquest through the 20th century. Topics include colonialism, slavery, monoculture, United States-Caribbean relations, and decolonization.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Cuba
courses.description: Thematic approach to Cuban history, from conquest to the revolution. Attention is given to socioeconomic developments, slavery and race relations, the 19th-century independence process, and the 20th-century republic.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Slavery and the US Civil War
courses.description: A comparative examination of the movements, experiences, and contributions of Africans and people of African descent from the period of the Atlantic slave trade to the present. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Women and Gender in African History
courses.description: Analysis of historical transformations in Africa and their effects on women's lives and gender relations. Particular themes include precolonial societies, colonialism, religious change, urban labor, nationalism, and sexuality. Honors version available.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Revolution in the Modern Middle East
courses.description: This course will focus on revolutionary change in the Middle East during the last century, emphasizing internal social, economic, and political conditions as well as international contexts.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Women in the Middle East
courses.description: Explores the lives of women in the Middle East and how they have changed over time. Focus will change each year.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Middle East and the West
courses.description: This course explores changing interactions between the Middle East and the West, including trade, warfare, scientific exchange, and imperialism, and ends with an analysis of contemporary relations in light of the legacy of the past.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Economic History of Southeast Asia
courses.description: This course is intended as a broad overview of Southeast Asian economic history from premodern times to the present day.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Gender in Chinese History
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce undergraduates to recent historical scholarship in the field of Chinese gender studies. Topics include family and kinship, the body and bodily practices, social space, writing, sexuality, work, and law, covering both the premodern and modern periods. No prior coursework required.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Fiction and History in India
courses.description: This course examines the histories, representations, and cultural perceptions surrounding bandits and rebels in modern India. The representations of bandits and rebels are studied in the light of the emergence of nationalism, shifting notions of gender and masculinity, race relations, and emergence of capitalist structures.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Oral History and Performance
courses.description: This course combines readings and field work in oral history with the study of performance as a means of interpreting and conveying oral history texts. Honors version available.

source.text: HIST 562. | 3 Credits. | HI-PERFORM. | COMM 562 , FOLK 562 , WGST 562 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Religion, Race, and Inquisition in the Spanish Empire
courses.description: This course on the "Atlantic World" studies Muslims, Christians, and Jews in the medieval Iberian kingdoms, then the religious "other" in the colonial expansion to Latin America, by deploying theories concerning race, gender, sexuality, and postcoloniality.

source.text: HIST 564. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER, RESEARCH. | RELI 564 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Civil War and Reconstruction, 1848-1900
courses.description: Focus is on causes, nature, and consequences of the Civil War.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The History of Sexuality in America
courses.description: A history of the sexual practices, desires, and understandings of Americans, from earliest colonial encounters to the late 20th century.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Women in the South
courses.description: An exploration of the distinctive themes in Southern women's lives, using the evidence of history and literature.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Vietnam War
courses.description: A wide-ranging exploration of America's longest war, from 19th-century origins to 1990s legacies, from village battlegrounds to the Cold War context, from national leadership to popular participation and impact.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Southern Music
courses.description: Explores the history of music in the American South from its roots to 20th-century musical forms, revealing how music serves as a window on the region's history and culture.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Ethnohistory of Native American Women
courses.description: Introduces students to the study of Native American women through the perspectives of anthropology, history, and autobiography.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: United States Foreign Relations in the 20th Century
courses.description: How the United States came to occupy a leading role in world affairs as a diplomatic, military, economic, and cultural power and what that role has meant to Americans and to other peoples, especially during the Cold War.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Transatlantic Relations and Contemporary Geo-Politics from the Cold War to the Present
courses.description: This course considers transatlantic relations in its security, political, and economic dimensions. The course also analyzes U.S. attempts to construct a more united European continent. It is the main aim of this course to give students a structured overview of transatlantic relations and geo-political developments from 1945 to the present.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: International Relations and Public History
courses.description: The course combines an academic and practical approach to policy formulation, implementation, and critical evaluation at the global level and based on a solid historical foundation. This course is tightly integrated with the UNC Krasno Global Events Series. Many of the talks in the series as well as the reading material in preparation deal with issues of 20th history, such as the Cold War years, US foreign policy, America's relations with the wider world.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: American Constitutional History to 1876
courses.description: In a classroom environment characterized by discussion, simulation, and interaction, the antecedents, formation, and interpretation of the Constitution are confronted in a broad historical matrix.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: American Constitutional History since 1876
courses.description: Using a classroom environment similar to HIST 581 , constitutional adjustments and change are related to psychological, political, social, and economic factors, and to Supreme Court members.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The Promise of Urbanization: American Cities in the 19th and 20th Centuries
courses.description: A survey of the development of American cities since 1815 and their influence upon American history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Race, Basketball, and the American Dream
courses.description: This course explores how Americans have used basketball for integration, economic mobility, and political protest. Particular focus is on how black Americans have used the game for individual expression and political and economic advancement; and the ways the game has influenced ideas about race, "whiteness," and "blackness" in our society.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The New South
courses.description: This course explores the transformation of the South from the time of the Civil War and emancipation to the contemporary rise of the Sunbelt.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Race, Racism, and America: (United States) Law in Historical Perspective
courses.description: This course will historically and critically examine the changing legal status of people of color in the United States. Within a broad historical matrix from the colonial era to the present, it will focus on African Americans, Native Americans, Asian Americans, Latina/os, and United States law.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Exploring the U.S. South Hands On and Ears Open: Internship at the Southern Oral History Program
courses.description: The Southern Oral History Program offers experiential education in the intellectual, organizational, and practical work of oral history. You will learn to do oral history interviews, contribute to a collaborative research project, and help this esteemed research center with programming, processing interviews, communications, and digital projects. You must apply through the Southern Oral History Program. This course is application-only.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introduction to Oral History
courses.description: Introduces students to the uses of interviews in historical research. Questions of ethics, interpretation, and the construction of memory will be explored, and interviewing skills will be developed through field work.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introduction to Public History
courses.description: Introduces the theory, politics, and practice of historical work conducted in public venues (museums, historic sites, national parks, government agencies, archives), directed at public audiences, or addressed to public issues.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Writing for a Popular Audience
courses.description: A seminar on the art of translating academic expertise for a general audience. Students read model works ranging from philosophy to biology, workshop story ideas, and learn how to publish in print and online media. Open to all disciplines.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Honors in History
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Introduction to the methods of historical research; designed to lead to the completion of an honors essay.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Honors in History
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Introduction to the methods of historical research; designed to lead to the completion of an honors essay.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Thinking Historically
courses.description: Introduces students to the intellectual currents and schools of thought that have characterized the historical profession over time. By examining such diverse conceptual frameworks, students will prepare themselves to tackle more confidently the research projects they will design and execute in HIST 900 and 901 .

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introduction to Medieval and Early Modern Studies
courses.description: This is an interdisciplinary course to introduce graduate students to the sources, methods, and approaches of medieval studies.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introduction to Historical Education
courses.description: Provides an introduction to teaching history. Topics include the history of historical education, planning a course, the role of the teacher, goals and methods, using new technologies, and evaluating students.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Professional Lives of Historians
courses.description: In this course, students explore the many identities of professional historians. Through readings and assignments, students learn about the state and future of the historical profession, develop skills that will serve them in their careers, and identify their own goals as professional historians and/or public intellectuals.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introductory Colloquium on Early Modern Europe
courses.description: Directed readings on early European history, from Britain through European Russia.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introductory Colloquium on Modern Europe
courses.description: Directed readings on modern European history, from Britain through European Russia.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introductory Colloquium in Latin American History before 1810
courses.description: Directed readings on Latin American history from preconquest to 1810; required for students entering the field.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introductory Colloquium in the History of Latin America since 1810
courses.description: Directed readings on Latin American history in the National Period; required for students entering the field.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introduction to Military History
courses.description: An introduction to the methods, issues, and literature of military history, including classic works and scholarship representative of a variety of approaches from history and other disciplines.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in African History
courses.description: An introduction to major works and themes in the history of premodern and modern African history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introduction to Asian History
courses.description: An introduction to major works and themes in the history of Asia with an emphasis on the history of China, Japan, and South Asia.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of the Atlantic World, 1400-1800
courses.description: Examines the changing economic, political, and cultural dynamics between and across Europe, Africa, and the Americas with special attention to colonization and slavery. The course is intended to familiarize students with major works in the field and the latest scholarship.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in Contemporary Global History
courses.description: Focus on the 19th and 20th centuries. Mixing theory, case studies, and comparisons, the readings reflect disciplinary diversity.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in Global Cold War History
courses.description: A historiographical overview of the Cold War in a global context, 1945-1991. The course familiarizes students with major works in the field and the latest scholarship.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in U.S. Immigration History
courses.description: This graduate seminar assumes basic knowledge of U.S. immigration history, allowing us to delve into the legal and administrative history of immigration restriction. Centered on the history of state power, this course examines the development of laws, policies, and institutions that, while often separate from voluntary migration, are deeply interconnected with it. Special emphasis will be placed on the intersections between structural nativism and American racism, particularly as they relate to the evolving forms of White supremacy. Throughout the seminar, we will explore works that uncover these intersections in unexpected arenas.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Selected Readings in the Comparative or Global History of Women and Gender
courses.description: Readings in the history of women and gender in a comparative, global, or transnational perspective.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introductory Colloquium in United States History to 1788
courses.description: Directed readings on American history from the precolonial period through the American Revolution; required for students entering the field.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introductory Colloquium in United States History, 1788 to 1900
courses.description: Directed readings on American history from the Constitution through the end of the nineteenth century; required for students entering the field.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introductory Colloquium in United States History since 1900
courses.description: Directed readings on American history in the twentieth century; required for students entering the field.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Feminist and Gender Theory for Historians
courses.description: Readings in contemporary feminist and gender theory, focused especially on theories that address the construction, writing, and general practice of history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in the History of Sexuality and Gender
courses.description: Readings on the historical study of gender and sexuality and on definitions of femininity and masculinity in different historical contexts.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Women, Gender and Sexuality: Historiography and Method
courses.description: This course will examine the origins, growth, and maturation of a field whose initial explorations sought simply to identify women's contributions to history, then began to conceptualize gender as a system that organized social relations, and most recently, has interrogated sexuality as practice and identity.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Graduate Readings in History of Law and Society
courses.description: Introduces students to the study of law and society across world regions and time periods. Students will explore historical meaning of legal institutions and processes in social, political, and cultural contexts. Explores terms and concepts of legal history such as rule of law, legal pluralism, sovereignty, consent, and justice.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in the History of Science and Medicine
courses.description: Examines the principal historiographical problems in the history of science and medicine, focusing on a different topic each year.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History and Memory: An Introduction into Theory, Methodology, and Research
courses.description: This graduate seminar explores the theory, methodology, and scholarship on history and memory, and examines some broad questions about the importance of studying collective memory. We will seek to understand both, different theoretical and methodological approaches, and their practical use in historical research and writing.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Politics of Human Rights in Global Perspective
courses.description: This seminar explores the politics of human rights by examining practices of rights-claiming since the early modern period. Taking a global perspective, it examines varying and contested modalities of agency in articulating rights in the name imagined group identities (nation, religion, or civilization), sex, the individual, and the human.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History and the Social Sciences
courses.description: The relationship of the social sciences to history, logic of inquiry, use of quantitative methods, and introduction to the computer.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Getting the Archive to Speak
courses.description: In this introduction to the problem of the archive in theory and practice, we will consider basic challenges historians have confronted over the past half-century, examples of the resulting research strategies, and their advantages and limitations. What constitutes rigorous, ethical historical practice? How can we interpret fragmentary, partial, or misleading sources? What stories can - and should - we try to tell? We will draw on notable works in the historiographies of Africa, Europe, Asia, the Americas.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Problems in Greek History, 600-323 BCE
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. This course introduces graduate students to problems in the use of literary, epigraphic, and archaeological sources for a range of issues, including religion, law, and warfare.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Rome, 27 BCE-180 CE
courses.description: Readings, reports, and discussions on selected topics of current importance for the field. Topics to be announced in advance.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in Medieval and Early Modern Women's History
courses.description: A readings course on the history of women, gender, and sexuality in Medieval Europe.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Late Medieval England
courses.description: Readings in English history, ca. 1300-1500, with a focus on social, economic, political, and legal topics.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Europe in the 16th Century
courses.description: A survey of the best historical literature emphasizing churches, varieties of secular power, and religious practice.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in Early Modern European History
courses.description: Selected readings and discussion of topics and relevant historiography in early modern Europe.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Early Modern Germany
courses.description: A topical survey of the political, social, and economic history of early modern Germany.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Problems in the History of the French Revolution
courses.description: Readings, reports, and discussion on aspects of the French Revolutionary upheaval in Europe.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in Modern European Women's and Gender History
courses.description: A readings course in the history of women in Europe since 1500.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Topics in Modern European History
courses.description: This course examines particular themes, events, and historiographical debates of Modern European History in a seminar setting.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in the Intellectual History of Europe
courses.description: A readings course on specific themes and debates in modern European intellectual life.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in European Social History
courses.description: This graduate readings course discusses classic works as well as recent landmark books about the development of European society in the 19th and 20th centuries.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in Modern European History, 1918-1945
courses.description: Directed readings, varying from year to year, selected from historiographical classics as well as the most recent scholarly publications.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Studies in Modern English History
courses.description: Directed readings in 19th- and 20th-century English history. Topics vary from year to year.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Topics in French History
courses.description: Open to graduate students from all departments. This course examines one period or one set of problems within French history since the Renaissance. Topics determined by instructor.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Colonialism and European Visual Culture, 1800-1990
courses.description: Considers the role of visual representation in the construction of European empire and its associated knowledges from the Napoleonic expedition to Egypt to debates over primitivism in the 1980s.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in Russian History, 1796-1917
courses.description: Selected readings and discussion of various topics in the history of Russia from the late 18th century to the Russian Revolution.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in Soviet History
courses.description: A historiographical reading colloquium covering Soviet and post-Soviet Russian history, 1917-present. The course familiarizes students with Western, Soviet, and post-Soviet literature on the most important issues in Soviet history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Introduction to Russian, Eurasian, and East European History
courses.description: This interdisciplinary seminar provides an in-depth look at some of the major topics in modern Russian, East European, and Eurasian history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in East European History
courses.description: Directed readings on modern East European history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in Modern Central Asian History
courses.description: The peoples of Islamic Central Eurasia are united by linguistic, cultural, and religious ties. Their history is divided between study fields: Soviet/Russian, Chinese, and Islamic Studies. Course takes historiographical diversity as a point of departure, interrogating the major debates that have animated the study of Islamic Central Asia across disciplines.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Colonial Encounters
courses.description: This course introduces students to a variety of theoretical and methodological approaches to the study of colonialism. It encourages them to examine critically the ways in which scholars apply and use the concepts of "coloniality" and "postcoloniality," and to assess the avenues through which those concepts might prove to be productive in informing their own research.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of Muslim Societies in Asia and Africa
courses.description: This graduate course will examine the intellectual, political and cultural history of Muslim societies since 1492 through the methodology and approaches of global history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Topics in African History
courses.description: A readings-based course on particular topics or approaches in African history. Topics may vary by semester and will be announced in advance.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Topics in Asian History
courses.description: Instructors use this course to focus on particular topics or historical approaches related to Asian history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Problems in Latin American History
courses.description: Instructors use this course to focus on particular topics or approaches in Latin American history. Topics to be announced in advance.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Biography and Memoir in Modern Latin American History
courses.description: This graduate seminar examines the role of biography and memoir in national-period Latin American historiography.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in Early American History
courses.description: Selected readings and research in United States history and its multicultural dimensions up to the American Revolution.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The United States in the Federal Period, 1789-1820
courses.description: Readings, discussion, and book lists designed to give familiarity with the historiographical problems, research opportunities, and bibliography of the period.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: The United States in the Middle Period, 1815-1860
courses.description: An analysis of the material and ideological transformations within the antebellum republic, which climaxed in the sectional crisis of the 1850s.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in the Antebellum South
courses.description: A review of traditional and modern literature on the pre-Civil War South, focusing on the interrelationships of its economy, society, culture, and politics.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Civil War and Reconstruction, 1860-1876
courses.description: An intensive readings course on key works comprising the core historiography for Civil War-Reconstruction America. Discussions, short papers, and a 20-page historiographical paper comprise the bulk of the assignments.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in the South since Reconstruction
courses.description: Readings, reports, and discussions on selected topics with a view to gaining familiarity with the literature of the field.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Political and Social History of Modern America
courses.description: A course of readings for advanced students that relate social history to the history of the state in America in the period from the Great Depression and the New Deal to the present.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in United States Labor History
courses.description: A graduate reading seminar on the history of America's workers from the 20th century to the present. The struggle of American workers to achieve a measure of dignity and security is examined from social, economic, and political perspectives. The course critically evaluates recent scholarship in the field of labor history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Colloquium in United States Military History
courses.description: Reading colloquium in United States military history focusing on the most significant issues, methods, and approaches in the field today.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: History of United States Foreign Relations
courses.description: Readings and research exploring various topics in modern American foreign relations and diplomacy.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in Urban History
courses.description: A readings course to introduce students to the main topics in urban history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: 19th and 20th Century American Labor History
courses.description: Graduate reading seminar in American labor history intended for students doing research as well as those writing M.A. and doctoral theses. Graduate students from fields other than United States history welcome. Students will read texts and articles by scholars in a wide variety of fields of American labor history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in United States Women's and Gender History
courses.description: A readings course on the history of women and gender in the United States.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in African American History
courses.description: Graduate students compile bibliographies and read important contributions to various aspects of African American history, stressing shifts in African American historiography and including very recent works.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Topics in American Cultural History
courses.description: Research seminar exploring various topics in United States cultural history to be announced in advance.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in Native American History
courses.description: Readings in and discussions of the major works in Native American history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Readings in the Global History of Capitalism
courses.description: This course exposes graduate students to the classical and burgeoning debates among historians over the history of global capitalism around the world from its antecedents in the medieval and early modern period until the present.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Topics in History for Graduates
courses.description: Instructors use this course to focus on particular topics or historical approaches. Specific course descriptions are available each semester on the departmental Web site (www.unc.edu/depts/history).

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Independent Study for Graduate Students
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Independent reading programs for graduate students whose needs are covered by no course immediately available. For students resident in Chapel Hill or vicinity.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Crafting a Historical Project
courses.description: Intended to help students develop a plan of research and writing, select a bibliography, develop an understanding of the literature available for their topic, and articulate a problem or facet of the topic to which they can contribute original research in their M.A. thesis.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: M.A. Research Seminar
courses.description: A seminar for those preparing the M.A. thesis. Pursuing original research in primary sources, students prepare full drafts of their theses.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Writing for Historians: A Seminar on the Craft of Historical Writing
courses.description: Doctoral students focus intensively on the writing process to produce an article-length piece of work suitable for publication. Topics include quotation, translation, narrative technique, structuring argument, and addressing a wide audience.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Dissertation Design
courses.description: Required of all doctoral candidates in the last semester of course work, this practicum helps students refine a dissertation topic and produce a prospectus.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Dissertation Seminar
courses.description: A seminar for A.B.D. students, offered as demand and resources permit.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Ancient History
courses.description: Research seminar on selected topics of current importance for the field. Topics to be announced in advance.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Medieval Dissertation Design
courses.description: This course complements HIST 905 , focusing on specific skills, sources, and methods for designing a dissertation prospectus in the field of medieval European history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Historiography and Narrative: Ancient, Medieval and Early Modern
courses.description: This course involves the close study of narrative historiographical texts before 1700. It introduces students to narratological approaches to textual analysis as well as to scholarly work, in a variety of disciplines, on the question of memory. The course is interdisciplinary in its orientation.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Research Seminar in African History
courses.description: Intended to accommodate students at various stages in their graduate careers, this multipurpose seminar will focus on problems in modern African history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Seminar in Modern European History
courses.description: This writing seminar explores the process of working with primary sources, creating a narrative, and shaping an interpretation based on examples from the last two centuries of European history.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Seminar in Russian and East European History
courses.description: A multi-purpose writing seminar on Russian and Soviet history in which students may write a seminar paper, M.A. thesis, dissertation prospectus, or dissertation chapter.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: American Revolution, 1763-1789
courses.description: Research seminar exploring various topics related to United States history in the late 18th century around the time of the American Revolution.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Research in Native American History
courses.description: This course introduces graduate students to research methods in Native American history, including the methodology of ethnohistory and the techniques of compiling a source base, taking notes, and outlining.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Research Seminar in Military History
courses.description: Introduction to research that should result in a major research product. Students will alternate reading classic texts in military history with discussions of project conceptualization and research strategies.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Advanced Seminar in Military History
courses.description: A research seminar designed to bring major projects (usually an M.A. thesis) to completion.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Seminar in Latin American History
courses.description: All students will be required to complete an original research paper based on use of primary sources on a Latin American topic corresponding to the theme of the seminar to be announced in advance.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Seminar in Women's and Gender History
courses.description: Writing seminar for graduate students on all levels who work on the history of women and gender.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Seminar in History
courses.description: Given on demand and as resources permit, this seminar allows faculty to respond to student interest in particular topics.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Master's Research and Thesis
courses.description: Individual work on the M.A . thesis, pursued under the supervision of the M.A. advisor.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: Doctoral Research and Dissertation
courses.description: Individual work on the doctoral dissertation, pursued under the supervision of the Ph.D. advisor.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.
